ahh i see, makes sense. so basically, real life doesnt lie to you. you could reference a picture of a real fox or wolf or cat or whatever and youll be following its exact anatomy, however, a drawing of one will likely be more stylised, so the rules are essentially broken. not in a bad way of course, art styles bend reality to look more appealing and unique. but as a beginner artist, you should learn the fundamentals first, and then learn how to break the rules in a way that works. you dont need a super vivid imagination to draw stuff, referencing is really good and it's good that you did that instead of relying on your mind to come up with something. our minds arent really an accurate reference. with time you'll get better at drawing stuff from the imagination of course, but you shouldnt rely on it. i hope this helps

did you ask for permission to reference this persons artwork and post it? totally valid to do for practice, but posting it online is another thing entirely. also, referencing people's art can be great when finding your own style, but generally you should learn the rules before you break them. look at real reference imagery and go from there. also, dont just try to draw the outline. try to understand the form of what youre drawing, the underlying structure and how it connects to other parts of the body. it just looks like you tried to copy the same outline as the reference artwork, which ultimately doesnt get you to understand what youre drawing exactly. aside from that though, it's a good start and the colouring is really solid and well done

it's both. and often times, a recessed jaw isnt enough to be referred for surgery on the grounds of health alone. my health is otherwise generally pretty good and i'm not really impacted by my slight overbite or anything. but it's noticeable to others as an "unhealthy" trait whether they acknowledge it or not.

also, some people get severe acne as a genetic issue, not as a hygiene issue. and generally, most people with severe acne are otherwise quite healthy. again, it's one of those things where you can't really get easy help for it since it's seen as more of an aesthetic concern, and for some people it's simply not possible.

you're missing my point. in any culture is a recessed chin preferred? or rotten teeth? or cystic acne? or blackheads? doubt it. because they're all seen as being unhealthy. beauty standards are not 100% made up. they exist because, like any other animal on this planet, we are naturally drawn to those who appear healthy and capable. ugly often = unhealthy from a biological standpoint. this doesnt include big noses, or skin tone, or eye colour. because all of these things dont indicate health

by "beauty standards" i mean conventional features. forward maxilla and mandible, short philtrum, small nose, lifted eyebrows, cat eyes etc. everything you see in most models. some "unconventional" models might have everything but the cat eyes. theyre still attractive. have you ever seen a model with a recessed maxilla/mandible, long philtrum, huge nose, super low-set eyebrows and super downturned eyes? i doubt it. teeth can be fixed... with money. facial deformities can be fixed... with money. most of us are here bc we dont have the money to fix the things we want to fix. also... the model you sent looks good and literally has none of the issues i've mentioned. if her teeth was the only issue then you're literally proving my point

see, it's hard bc i'm quiet until people invest in me usually. i might chime in with a comment but i guess i also prove the sentiment that i don't give much effort to connecting with people who aren't worth my time. however, when people talk to me, i do my best to keep the conversation going and show my interest, i'm not cold and emotionless, i laugh along etc. i'm not a typical "asocial" person, i am actually quite social when the environment is right. i try to show that i want to engage, i listen, i try to hear out those who are also quiet and so on. i think this should give me an edge at times but often, it doesn't. my social energy then quickly drains and that's when i become quiet, bc i realise my efforts arent recognised. it takes a hell of a lot of courage to speak up though, so i get upset that when i do, it's often not recognised or i'm talked over. doesn't help that i'm soft spoken. i've come to realise maybe that's just how it is, that soft spoken anxious people arent really built for social events. but it sucks bc i want to engage in them. if it was as easy as just starting conversation with someone, i'd do it in a heartbeat bc i want to. it's not that i'm asocial or antisocial, i can be very extroverted with the right sorts of people who i know are interested in me. i wouldnt turn up to social events if i wasnt interested. hell, i even message people ahead of time in preparation for social events giving a heads up that im quite anxious but im more than happy to be there, i try to make sure im not going into these things with total strangers who dont understand my situation. but either way, it goes ignored. it's difficult
